verdict: Franklin Templeton's revenue rose just 4% to $2.43B, but profit jumped as last year's $202M intangible-asset impairment did not repeat and gains inside its consolidated funds more than doubled other income.

kpis.label: Long-term net inflows
kpis.note: new client money, net, in the quarter

segments.name: Investment management fees
segments.note: Fees charged as a percentage of the $1.8T Franklin manages for clients — 80% of revenue, up 4% as markets and inflows lifted assets.

segments.name: Sales and distribution fees
segments.note: Fees tied to selling and distributing its funds — up 6%.

segments.name: Shareholder servicing fees
segments.note: Fees for servicing fund shareholders' accounts — down 5%.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.note: Everything else — down 26%, a tiny slice of revenue.

opex.name: Compensation and benefits
opex.note: Pay and benefits — the biggest cost of running an asset manager, flat YoY.

opex.name: Information systems and technology
opex.note: Trading, data and technology systems — up 2%.

opex.name: Occupancy
opex.note: Offices around the world — flat YoY.

opex.name: Amortization of intangible assets
opex.note: Writing down the value of past acquisitions over time — down from $69M a year ago.

otherDetail: Investment and other income of $81M, plus $236M of income from consolidated investment products — funds Franklin consolidates onto its own books — less $31M of interest expense and $8M of consolidated-product expenses: $278M net. Much of the fund income belongs to outside investors in those funds, which is why $174M of net income is attributable to noncontrolling interests.
oneTimers: No impairment charge this quarter. A year ago Franklin booked a $202M impairment of intangible assets, which is the main reason GAAP operating income rose 317% YoY.

Adjusted (non-GAAP) operating income was $599M and adjusted EPS was $0.94; the adjusted figures exclude amortization and impairment of intangibles, the consolidated investment products and certain other items. GAAP EPS was $0.72.
Of the $554M of consolidated net income, $174M belonged to noncontrolling interests — outside investors in consolidated funds. Net income attributable to Franklin Templeton shareholders was $380M.

takeaways.title: Client money is flowing in again
takeaways.text: Long-term net inflows were $20.8B in the quarter and $84.1B for the fiscal year, with inflows in every quarter and across equity, multi-asset and alternatives. Assets under management reached $1,795B, up 8% YoY.

takeaways.title: Operating income jumped — mostly an easy comparison
takeaways.text: Operating income rose to $356M from $85M, but a year ago the quarter carried a $202M intangible-asset impairment. On Franklin's adjusted basis, operating income rose a more modest 27% to $599M.

takeaways.title: Alternatives are the growth corner
takeaways.text: Alternative assets — private markets and other non-traditional strategies — reached a record $305B, with $48.7B raised during the fiscal year, as Franklin pushes beyond traditional stock and bond funds.

footerNote: An asset manager reports no cost of goods sold. This page treats Sales, distribution and marketing expense ($560M) — the cost of distributing its funds — as the direct-cost step; the remaining operating expenses, operating income ($356M) and net income ($554M) then match the release exactly. Franklin labels these results preliminary.
